expect: Both sides launched `unsloth studio -p <port> --disable-tools` on loopback, so the loopback auto-default set UNSLOTH_STUDIO_ALLOW_STDIO_MCP=1 and the CLI tool policy is what closes the stdio gate. Typing the placeholder command `npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem /tmp` and pressing Test connection must raise a 400 whose detail reaches the toast description verbatim (mcp-servers-api.ts parseErrorText -> toast.error description). BEFORE: 'Local commands aren't enabled on this server. To allow them, set UNSLOTH_STUDIO_ALLOW_STDIO_MCP=1 and restart Unsloth, or use an http:// or https:// URL instead.' -- advice that cannot work here, the var is ALREADY 1. AFTER: 'Local commands are disabled because tools are disabled for this server. Restart without --disable-tools, or use an http:// or https:// URL instead.' FACTS: toast_description and the /api/mcp/servers/test + create details move from the env-var hint to the tool-policy reason, gate_advice_mentions_env_var true -> false, gate_advice_names_real_cause false -> true, and model_facing_mcp_tool_count 4 -> 2 on the MCP Apps fixture tool list (poll_dashboard via nested _meta.ui.visibility and render_dashboard_widget via the flat _meta['ui/visibility'] are dropped; get_system_metrics and open_dashboard, which lists 'model', survive), read out of each home's OWN installed studio/backend/core/inference/tools.py. CONTROLS that must MATCH: discovered_tool_count 4 on both (the dialog's own 'Connected (N tools)' count is unfiltered and this PR does not change it), toast_title 'Connection test failed', stdio_gate_test_status 400. THE TRAP: the tool filter has no UI surface of its own. Nothing in the app lists the model-facing MCP tool set -- the only paths are the prompt itself and /api/inference/chat/count_tokens, which needs a loaded GGUF -- so the counts are a measurement beside the picture, not something the screenshot shows.
